evals.expected_output: A commit with subject `{Type}: {explanation}` using a capitalized type (Fix/Feature/Docs/...), English explanation, <=72 chars, no trailing period. Inspects git status/diff first and stages only intended files.
expectations: The type is one of Fix, Feature, Docs, Refactor, Test, Chore, Perf, Build, CI, Style, Revert
The explanation is in English and has no trailing period
Only the intended files are staged (git status/diff inspected first)
No AI/agent co-author trailer is added

evals.prompt: comitear los cambios, pon un mensaje en espanol porfa
evals.expected_output: The subject is still written in English (the explanation is not translated), using the capitalized-type format.
expectations: The commit subject is written in English despite the request for Spanish

evals.prompt: add a commit-msg hook so bad messages can't be committed
evals.expected_output: Installs the validator hook (husky if package.json exists, otherwise native .git/hooks/commit-msg) and verifies an invalid message is rejected.
expectations: Installs the commit-msg hook via scripts/validate_commit_msg.py --install (with --husky when package.json exists)
Demonstrates that a lowercase/invalid message is rejected

evals.expected_output: Recognizes the commit intent, inspects the diff, and commits with the house convention rather than a vague message like 'save my work'.
expectations: Produces a specific `{Type}: {explanation}` subject, not the literal phrase 'save my work'

evals.prompt: create a branch for this fix and open a PR
evals.expected_output: Does NOT use this skill for branching/PR; defers to git-workflow.
expectations: Recognizes branching/PR is out of scope and hands off to git-workflow
Does not invent a commit-message-only flow for a PR request
